name: spells

attributes.attribute: verbal magic that can heal or harm
believed to hold power over the world through speech
the heart of a spell, more than any rite

sources: Campbell, John Grigorson. Witchcraft and Second Sight in the Highlands and Islands of Scotland. Detroit: Singing Tree Press, 1970, 57.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A spell is a ritual action. It is verbal magic. The Celts believed a bard could change the physical world by the strength of speech. In folklore this grew into the idea that a rhyming spell can heal or harm. Words used as a blessing heal. Words used as a curse harm. A brief rite sometimes joined the rhyme, such as dipping stones in water or rubbing the body. That rite sat below the rhyme itself in worth. The spoken verse did the real work.
